judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Any of the following, among other restrictions' places an unbounded catch-all alongside a closed bulleted list, which is precisely the general-versus-specific problem; 'salaries or bonuses' paid 'directly' also leaves indirect payments untouched.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: 'Majority in Interest' is defined here as more than 50% of aggregate outstanding principal, whereas c095 requires more than 50% of principal plus accrued interest excluding affiliates — two different consent thresholds; the Lien bullet also excepts liens 'permitted pursuant to the Security Agreement', which c108 says may prime the Noteholders.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'May form one or more new funds ... or similar enterprises to the Company' is missing a word and reads incoherently; 'such of its business time ... as may be necessary' is an unmeasurable standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c056 states the same time commitment as 'only so much time to the business of the Company as is reasonably required', a different formulation of the same duty.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: 'Timely information reasonably necessary for the preparation of income tax returns' is the only hard obligation; everything else is at the Manager's discretion, so the reporting duty has almost no content.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is consistent with c112's promise of Form 1099s and with c018; no conflicting reporting obligation appears elsewhere.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear allocation of all tax items to Members and none to Noteholders; the word 'only' in 'will receive IRS Form 1099's only on a timely basis' is misplaced but not misleading.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c018 and c123's debt characterisation, though c126 contemplates the IRS recharacterising Noteholders as members, in which case this allocation could not hold.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence is broken — 'may not be amended without the approval of a Majority in Interest of Noteholders (i) violates the Company's obligations ...' omits the words that would connect the condition, so the protection's trigger is unreadable.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to 'the Investor Documents', a term used nowhere else (the document defines 'Offering Documents' and 'Noteholder Agreements'), leaving the cross-reference without a referent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The 'Notwithstanding the foregoing' sentence lets an individual Noteholder waive 'any provision' as to his own Note with only the Manager's consent, which is in tension with the Majority in Interest requirement in the preceding sentence.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Read against c109's Restricted Actions and c095's Collateral Agent consent regime, the instrument gives three different consent mechanisms for altering Noteholder protections without saying which governs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The indemnity is carefully drafted with a conduct carve-out and an advancement undertaking; 'activities undertaken on behalf of the Company' is broad but standard.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The carve-out here is 'willful misconduct or gross negligence', while c048 describes the same Operating Agreement indemnity as excluding 'fraud, bad faith or willful misconduct' — a direct conflict on the standard of protected conduct.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A plain non-recourse statement limited to the Noteholder's purchase commitment; nothing ambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with c018 and c097's statement that Noteholders are not members; no conflict found.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The power of attorney is headed 'Noteholders' Powers of Attorney' but the operative words authorise execution of documents 'that the Members have expressly agreed to execute', naming the wrong class of person.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: c097 and c116 state expressly that Noteholders are not Members, so as written the Noteholders' power of attorney has no subject matter — an internal incoherence.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Counsel's name is misspelled ('Greenburg Traurig'), but the substance — that counsel represents the Company and Manager, not investors — is unambiguous.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A scope-limiting tax summary with a long exclusion list; nothing operative and nothing genuinely ambiguous.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A statutory-form Circular 230 legend; determinate.
